3. From the FIR, it emerges that accused--Raman Puri, Varun Puri, and Vikram Puri, are the Managing Director and Directors, respectively, of M/s Universal Build Well Pvt. Ltd. (UBPL), and are also the promoters of the said company.

Accused persons, in connivance with each other,
entered into agreements to sell flats/dwelling units with various persons and began collecting booking amounts, followed by raising further demands, even prior to obtaining of building plan approval from the Town and Country Planning Department, Haryana.

The project was advertised in violation of the condition in Licence No. 51 of 2011 by way of newspaper publications and through 13 of 19 CRM-M-52795-2025(O&M) and other connected cases 14 property dealers.

It is alleged that there was never any intention on the part of the accused persons to hand over possession of the properties agreed to be sold and that their sole intention was to usurp the money of the investors.
Lured by the advertisements issued by the accused persons in respect of the project of their company, the investors, including the complainants/victims in the present case(s), invested their money.

4. Learned Senior Counsel further argued that petitioner is in custody for a period of last about 8/9-10 months and that due to the failure of the scheme to develop the business enterprise, the project went into doldrums, resulting in financial losses to the accused company.

It was further contended that during the pendency of the proceedings, a Resolution Professional has already been appointed for the company in question and, therefore, it cannot be claimed that the offences under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC are prima facie made out.

5. It has also been pointed out that in respect of the same project, petitioner has been facing several other FIRs containing similar allegations, and in many of those cases, petitioner--Varun Puri--has already been granted bail.

In this regard, learned Senior counsel places reliance upon the orders passed by the co-ordinate Bench(s) of this Court, the details of which are tabulated hereinbelow:

Learned Senior Counsel further argued that petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present cases, which are, in fact, purely civil in nature.
He submitted that although, petitioner is a builder but he is not a signatory to the confirmation of ownership.
He had signed the Builder-Buyer Agreement with the first buyer only in his capacity as an authorized signatory of UBPL and was a Director of UBPL at the relevant time.

Further submitted that once proceedings before the NCLT, Delhi have commenced and a Resolution Professional stood appointed, the assets were no longer under the control of either the petitioner or the company, as the same had been taken over by the Resolution Professional.
He also pointed out that although, there are total of about 64 FIRs against the petitioner and the allegations therein are identical and of a similar nature.

Petitioner, owing to procedural requirements, is compelled to seek bail separately in each case, despite the repeated 15 of 19 CRM-M-52795-2025(O&M) and other connected cases 16 allegations by different complainants/victims.
Thus, also in the light of all the aforementioned bail orders, learned Senior Counsel prays for grant of regular bail to the petitioner.

7. Per contra, Mr. P.K. Jhanda, learned Senior Deputy Advocate General, Haryana, opposed the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner and contended that petitioner is an habitual offender and is, in fact, involved in as many as 67 cases.

Upon a query by the Court as to whether petitioner's plea in all the aforementioned seven cases stands covered by the bail orders already passed (Annexures P-4 to P-7, P-3 and P-4 in CRM-M-64745- 2025) by Coordinate Benches of this Court, Mr. Pawan Kumar Jhanda, learned Senior DAG, Haryana, after examining the bail petitions and the referred orders, fairly conceded that factually all the cases, including the allegations levelled against the petitioner, are similar in nature.
